description: DDoS Attack on Public Endpoints Attackers can generate massive amounts of traffic targeting the public endpoints, potentially exhausting resources and preventing legitimate users from accessing the service. A botnet could be used to generate thousands of requests per second to the ALB or API Gateway endpoints, overwhelming the system's capacity to handle legitimate traffic.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1498 - Network Denial of Service
mitreATT&CK: T1499 - Endpoint Denial of Service
recommendation: Implement AWS Shield Advanced for DDoS protection
recommendation: Implement rate limiting at multiple layers

description: Single Point of Failure in Load Balancer Configuration If the ALB experiences issues or becomes overwhelmed, all incoming traffic would be affected as there's no redundancy in the load balancing layer. A targeted attack or technical failure affecting the ALB could disrupt all incoming traffic to the application, even if the backend services remain healthy.

Insecure Service-to-Service Communication Without a service mesh, services communicate directly over the network without enforced encryption or strong mutual authentication, potentially allowing unauthorized access or eavesdropping. An attacker who gains access to the VPC could potentially intercept inter-service communication or impersonate a service to gain unauthorized access to other services.

Inefficient Database Connection Management Each service instance creates its own database connections without pooling, potentially exhausting database connection limits during high load or attack scenarios. An attacker could trigger multiple rapid requests causing services to create many database connections, exhausting the connection pool and causing service disruption.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1499 - Endpoint Denial of Service
recommendation: Implement connection monitoring and alerting

description: Exposed AWS Service Endpoints Services accessing AWS APIs through public endpoints expose traffic to potential interception and make the system vulnerable to credential theft and unauthorized access. An attacker who compromises a service could potentially access AWS services through public endpoints, even if they gain access to valid credentials, as there's no network-level restriction.

description: Insufficient Secrets Management Sensitive credentials and configuration values might be exposed through environment variables or configuration files rather than being properly managed through Secrets Manager. An attacker who gains access to the ECS task definitions or environment variables could potentially extract sensitive credentials.
